name: Grammar And Clarity Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any grammar and clarity task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any grammar and clarity task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate grammar and clarity outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. When multiple grammar and clarity strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
3. Prefer the simplest grammar and clarity approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. When grammar and clarity guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Keep grammar and clarity outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen grammar and clarity approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Keep grammar and clarity changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
8. Measure before optimizing any grammar and clarity bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
9. When grammar and clarity decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
10. Check that grammar and clarity terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
11. Before starting grammar and clarity work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
12. State assumptions about grammar and clarity explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting grammar and clarity assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of grammar and clarity correctness.
- Do not silently drop grammar and clarity edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these grammar and clarity guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
